drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's four-cubit distance from feces apply in every direction, for Shema and for prayer?
outcomeNote: A single transmitted qualification of the mishna; no challenge in this unit (the next unit attacks it).

segments.he: כַּמָּה יַרְחִיק מֵהֶן וּמִן הַצּוֹאָה — אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת. אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לַאֲחוֹרָיו, אֲבָל לְפָנָיו — מַרְחִיק מְלֹא עֵינָיו, וְכֵן לִתְפִלָּה.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And, how far must one distance himself from urine and from feces» in order to recite Shema? «Four cubits. Rava said» that «Rav Seḥora said» that «Rav Huna said: They only taught» that it is sufficient to distance oneself four cubits when the feces are «behind him, but» if they are «before him he must distance himself» to the point that it is «no longer within his range of vision;» and the halakha «is the same» for «prayer.»

moves.cueHe: כמה ירחיק מהן ומן הצואה — ארבע אמות
moves.summary: The gemara quotes the mishna's lemma: one distances four cubits from urine and feces.
moves.about: the mishna's ruling that one distances four cubits from urine and feces

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא אמר רב סחורה אמר רב הונא: לא שנו אלא לאחוריו
moves.summary: Rav Huna (via Rav Seḥora and Rava) restricts the four cubits to feces behind him; before him one distances out of sight, and likewise for prayer.
moves.about: the four-cubit distance applies only to feces behind him; before him he must distance himself beyond his range of vision, and likewise for prayer
